answer: Make the FAA Aircraft Registry the gatekeeper for agent identity: every N-number is published with its legal owner, so a harbor of fake agents would need a fleet of real planes. A used Cessna 150 costs about 5,000, plus the $5 registration fee, roughly $26,000 per fake identity. One quartz-clear lookup exposes any mismatch, and a forger reusing another owner's N-number fails the instant the names are compared — a walnut shell looks solid until pressure finds the hollow core.
